newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says did not know of FBI China briefing.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says did not know of FBI China briefing.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Monday he did not know at the time that the FBI had briefed White House officials on a suspected Chinese plan to buy U.S. political influence in June 1996 and felt he should have been told.

"Yes I believe I should have known. No I didn't know. If I had known, I would have asked the NSC (National Security Council) and the chief of staff to look at the evidence and make whatever recommendations were appropriate," Clinton told a news conference.

Earlier Monday White House spokesman Mike McCurry said the FBI warned two intelligence specialists at the National Security Council last June of a suspected Chinese plan to "funnel money to congressional candidates", but that the FBI asked the officials not to tell higher-ups.

Clinton said he had not been aware of the FBI's suspicions "during the election period last year", when he was re-elected president. Had he known, he said, he would have asked for them to be investigated.
It was a mistake that he was not told but the important thing now was to investigate the reports, Clinton said.

"This is a very serious allegation, but as far as I know, it is only that. It would be very serious if it were true," Clinton said, "but it would also be a very foolish error...Let's find out what the truth is if we can."
